test.title: Test
test.subtitle: Complete tests by dimension to get your brain index
test.freeUserLimit: Free users can try one dimension (1-3 tests, about 15 minutes).

memory.nBackIntro1: This test presents a sequence of shapes or letters. You need to decide whether the current stimulus is the same as the one N steps before.
memory.cdIntro: A set of colored items is shown briefly, then shown again after a delay. Judge whether any item changed.
memory.sternbergIntro: Memorize a short set of items first. Then a probe item appears, and you decide whether it was in the set.
memory.sternbergPracticeDoneDesc: You have completed Sternberg practice. Start the formal test when ready.
memory.sternbergProbeQuestion: Was the probe item in the previous set?
memory.sternbergResultDesc: Below are the results of this Sternberg memory scanning test.
memory.cdPracticeDoneDesc: You have finished practice. Start the formal test when ready.
memory.cdResultDesc: Below are the results of this change detection test.
memory.practiceStreamHint: Stimuli play in sequence. Click Â«MatchÂ» when the current one matches N steps back.
memory.answerSameWhenMatch: Click Â«MatchÂ» when you think it matchesâ€”practice only, no scoring.
memory.practiceFeedbackWait: Wait until at least N stimuli are shown before judging.
memory.nBackPracticeDesc: Use the history and current stimulus to judge whether they match under the given N-back level. Once you are familiar, start the formal test.
memory.nBackFixedLevelHint: This test uses 2-back for all trials.
memory.nBackFormalDesc: For each trial, follow the shown N-back level and decide whether the current stimulus matches the one N steps earlier. Try to be both fast and accurate.
memory.nBackHintGrid: Grid mode: numbers in the 3Ã—3 grid represent different positions. Compare the current highlighted cell with the position {level} steps before.
memory.nBackHintLetter: Letter mode: letters are chosen from Aâ€“K. Compare the current letter with the one {level} steps before.
memory.nBackQuestion: Is the current stimulus the same as the {level}-back (the one {level} steps before)?
memory.nBackResultDesc: Below are the multi-metric results of this N-back test, used for later brain analysis and radar display.
memory.ageBandUnknown: Unclassified (missing age or out of range)
memory.displayScoreHint: Ability score combines dâ€² (hit rate and false-alarm rate) with correct-hit reaction time; Age percentile is an age-band norm estimate for training feedback only.

logic.patternDesc: Given relation chain, select the statement that must be true
logic.practiceDoneDesc: You have completed the practice item. Start the formal test when ready.
logic.practiceNoAnswer: Try one practice answer first (or start formal test directly)
logic.tiPrompt: Given the relation chain, determine the relation between two items
logic.tiCompareLine: Compare {left} and {right}: which statement must be true?
logic.tiFormalPrompt: Formal item: Given D > E, E > F. Which statement must be true?
logic.syllogismDesc: Given two premises, judge whether the conclusion must be true
logic.analogyDesc: Find the best option to complete the analogy relation

focus.flankerDesc: Judge the center arrow direction while ignoring surrounding distractors
focus.flankerShortcutHint: Quick controls: press â† for left and â†’ for right.
focus.flankerInstruction: Respond only to the center arrow direction
focus.schulteDesc: Tap targets in ascending order as quickly and steadily as possible
focus.stroopDesc: Select by font color, ignore word meaning
focus.stroopInstruction: Respond to the ink color, not the word meaning

reaction.title: Reaction Speed
reaction.desc: Click as soon as the screen changes color.
reaction.practiceDesc: Wait for the panel to turn green, then click immediately.
reaction.rulePractice: Start with one practice round to learn the timing.
reaction.ruleFormal: The formal test includes 5 scored trials.
reaction.ruleNoEarly: If you click before green appears, that round restarts.
reaction.ruleReference: Your score is adjusted using age-band reaction-time references.
reaction.practiceHint: You can repeat practice rounds before starting the formal test.
reaction.resultDesc: Your final score uses the median of 5 formal trials, plus best-trial and stability adjustments.
reaction.scoreHint: Reference ranges: teens 400-560 ms, young adults 190-250 ms, mid-age adults 250-350 ms, older adults 350-500 ms.
reaction.arrowDesc: When an arrow appears, press the matching direction key as fast as possible.
reaction.arrowPracticeDesc: Press the corresponding arrow key (↑ ↓ ← →) when the target appears.
reaction.arrowRulePractice: Start with practice rounds to get used to the timing.
reaction.arrowRuleFormal: The formal test includes 5 scored trials.
reaction.arrowRuleNoEarly: If you press before the arrow appears, that round restarts.
reaction.arrowRuleMatch: You must press the matching direction key; wrong key restarts the round.
reaction.arrowRuleReference: Your score is adjusted using age-group reaction-time references.
reaction.arrowPressNow: Press the matching arrow key now!
reaction.arrowPracticeHint: You can repeat practice rounds before starting the formal test.
reaction.pvtDesc: Watch the black frame and press Space as soon as the white dot appears to measure sustained vigilance and reaction stability.
reaction.pvtPracticeDesc: Press Space immediately when the white dot appears in the black frame. Practice repeats automatically.
reaction.pvtRulePractice: Start with practice rounds to adapt to random waiting intervals.
reaction.pvtRuleFormal: The formal test includes 5 scored trials.
reaction.pvtRuleNoEarly: Pressing Space before stimulus onset counts as a false start and restarts the round.
reaction.pvtRuleLapse: Reaction times above the age-band reference upper bound are counted as lapses and reduce the score.
reaction.pvtRuleReference: Scoring combines age-band norms, stability, and error penalties.
reaction.pvtWaiting: Stay alert and wait for the white dot...
reaction.pvtPressNow: White dot on, press Space now!
reaction.pvtPracticeHint: Keep practicing as needed, then start the formal test.

strategy.hanoiDesc: Move disks from the start peg to the target peg under strict rules to assess multi-step planning.
strategy.ruleOneDisk: Move only one disk at a time.
strategy.ruleNoLargeOnSmall: A larger disk cannot be placed on a smaller disk (illegal moves are counted).
strategy.rulePractice: Start with 1 practice trial (3 disks) to get familiar with controls.
strategy.ruleFormal: Formal test has 2 trials: trial 1 with 3 disks, trial 2 with 4 disks.
strategy.ruleAgeScoring: Final score is age-normalized by age-band benchmarks.
strategy.practiceHint: Goal: move all disks from Peg A to Peg C.
strategy.formalHint: Formal test: finish with fewer moves, fewer violations, and reasonable time.
strategy.illegalMove: Illegal move: a larger disk cannot be placed on a smaller disk.
strategy.londonDesc: Given a start state and goal state, complete the target in as few moves as possible with plan-first behavior.
strategy.londonRuleMoveOne: Move only one ball at a time, and only from the top of a peg.
strategy.londonRuleCapacity: Peg capacities are fixed at 3/2/1; moves beyond capacity count as rule violations.
strategy.londonRulePlanFirst: Observe the goal state first, then execute your plan.
strategy.londonRuleFormal: Formal phase has 3 trials: first 2 are 3-ball tasks, and trial 3 is a 4-ball task; final score uses the average.
strategy.londonRuleAgeScoring: Scoring is age-normalized using perfect-solution rate and initiation-time references.
strategy.londonIllegalCapacity: Illegal move: target peg capacity exceeded.
strategy.routeDesc: Plan and execute routes under constraints while balancing shortest distance and time efficiency.
strategy.routeRuleMove: Start from the start node and build your path step by step through adjacent nodes/cells.
strategy.routeRuleConstraint: You must satisfy constraints such as checkpoints and blocked nodes/edges.
strategy.routeRuleScoring: Scoring uses SPI: optimal-distance ratio, time efficiency, and complexity weight.
strategy.routeRuleFormal: Formal phase has 6 puzzles (3 grid + 3 graph).
strategy.routeFormalGraphTwo: Formal 5: Graph with Blocked Edge + Must Pass
strategy.routeReadySubmit: Path satisfies constraints. Ready to submit.
strategy.routeAutoSubmitAtGoal: Reaching G will auto-submit this trial.
strategy.routePracticeAutoStart: Practice completed. Formal test started automatically.
strategy.routePracticeNext: Practice solved. Switched to the next practice trial.
strategy.routePracticeAllDone: All practice trials completed. You can start the formal test.
strategy.routeNotReady: Start at S, pass required checkpoints, and end at G.
strategy.routeInvalidStep: Invalid step: only adjacent traversable links are allowed.
strategy.routeNoRevisit: Invalid step: previously visited cells/nodes cannot be visited again.
strategy.routeGoalAlreadyReached: Goal already reached. This trial has ended. Reset or continue.
strategy.routeGoalMissingCheckpoint: Goal reached without all required checkpoints. This trial is scored as failed.
strategy.routeNeedGoal: Current path does not meet submit conditions.
strategy.practiceDone: Practice completed. You can start the formal test.
strategy.practiceNotDone: Practice not completed yet. You can still start the formal test.

spatial.title: Spatial Imagination
spatial.desc: Decide if two shapes are the same after rotation
spatial.intro: You will see two 3D block shapes (A and B). Decide whether they are the same object viewed from a different angle, or if one is a mirror image.
spatial.introTip1: Same: B can be rotated in 3D to exactly match A
spatial.introTip2: Different: B is a mirror image of A — no rotation can make them match
spatial.question: Are these the same object?
spatial.resultDesc: Here are your spatial rotation test results.
spatial.resultScoreHint: Score combines accuracy (75%) and response speed (25%), max 100.
